propositions: A configured provider is silently dropped for any model id containing a colon because the qualified check was `":" in model`, and canonical versioned Bedrock ids contain a colon in their version suffix.
The dropped-provider failure surfaces late at LLM-call time as a misleading 'unknown provider' error naming a fragment of the model id, degrading the review gate to INDETERMINATE.

The qualified/unqualified decision was duplicated across `_resolve_target` and `infer_provider`, so both implementations drifted and failed the same way; they now route through one shared `split_provider_qualifier`.
An explicitly configured provider must be honored first, before any scan of the model string, so no punctuation can overrule it; a conflicting inline qualifier must raise rather than pick a winner.

The shipped fix uses an identifier-shape test rather than registered-provider-set membership, so a typo'd provider still passes silently; registry membership and the unknown-provider diagnostic are delegated to child 7b22.
The gate's existing fail-closed behavior on a genuine outage must remain unchanged, and no silent fallback to a default provider or cfg.model may be introduced.
